doc.name: Timefire Record
doc.instructions: Use these tools to inspect Timefire's resolved record. A book (the tools also say batch) is one trading day's full S&P 500 slate, normally graded ten trading days later. Resolved means graded. No tool returns a batch, ticker observation, or proof until that book is fully resolved. No API key is required.

tools.description:
List graded books, newest first, one summary row each: date, returns, alpha against SPY and RSP, and verdict.
    A book (or batch) is one trading day's full S&P 500 slate. Use this to find a trading_date, then get_resolved_batch
    for every forecast in that book or verify_batch for its proof. Dates with no graded book return an empty list.

limit.description: Most books to return, 1 to 500. Default 60.
limit.title: Limit

from_date.description: Earliest date to include, as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for no lower bound.
from_date.title: From Date

to_date.description: Latest date to include, as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for no upper bound.
to_date.title: To Date

tools.name: list_resolved_batches
tools.title: Book history

tools.description:
Get one graded book with every forecast and its outcome. A book (or batch) is one trading day's full S&P 500
    slate, served once its long picks are fully graded, so other rows can still have null outcomes. Use
    list_resolved_batches to find the date, verify_batch for the book's proof and get_book_portfolio for its portfolio.
    An ungraded or unknown date is an error.

trading_date.description: The book's trading date, as YYYY-MM-DD. list_resolved_batches gives the graded dates.
trading_date.title: Trading Date

tools.name: get_resolved_batch
tools.title: One book

tools.description:
Get aggregates computed only from fully resolved books: forecast counts, returns and hit rates, and how many
    books beat, matched (flat) or trailed SPY, each book's verdict graded on its cap-weighted long picks. The hit
    rates count the books graded under the published rule, from published_rule_from on; the 69 backtest books before
    it follow a rule of their own and are reported apart in the backtest_ fields, verdicts included. Use this for
    overall performance, get_calibration to test the ranking itself, and get_book_portfolio for a single book.
tools.name: get_track_record_stats
tools.title: Headline stats

tools.description:
Check whether forecasts matched outcomes: mean predicted against mean realized return by decile across every
    graded book, and hit rates by rank bucket and by side (long or short) across books graded under the published rule.
    Use this to judge how well the ranking held up, and get_track_record_stats for headline returns and the verdict
    tally.
tools.name: get_calibration
tools.title: Calibration

tools.description:
Get the versioned scoring rules, the metric definitions and the latest graded book's universe of stocks.
    Use this before interpreting a stat or a verdict, to learn how books are graded and which stocks are covered.
tools.name: get_universe_and_scoring_spec
tools.title: Record spec

tools.description:
Get one stock's rows from graded books only, newest first: its forecast, rank, pick side and outcome in each
    book. Use this to follow one ticker across books, explain_resolved_prediction for the evidence behind one row, and
    get_resolved_batch for a whole book. An unknown ticker returns an empty list.

ticker.description: Stock ticker, for example AAPL. Upper or lower case both work.
ticker.title: Ticker

limit.description: Most rows to return, 1 to 500. Default 120.
limit.title: Limit

tools.name: get_stock_resolved_history
tools.title: One stock's history

tools.description:
Get the public proof for one graded book: signed payload, hash, signature, content address and timestamp
    material, with the steps to check them. From 2026-04-28 on, a book is made after the close on its trading date
    (earlier books are a backtest, built later), and its return runs from that close over the next ten NYSE sessions
    (books before 2026-10-21 run from the first available close on or after that date over the next ten available
    sessions; the backtest books dated 2026-01-02 to 2026-04-13 run from the close before their date to nine sessions
    after it). The OpenTimestamps receipt proves the book existed before the Bitcoin block it names: compare that
    block's time with the next NYSE open after the trading date. sealed is true only while a book is still withheld.
    Every book served here is graded and revealed, so sealed is false, and that is not a failed check. The verified
    field is the server's own check of the hash and signature, not the timestamp; the evidence lets you repeat it
    yourself. Use this to check a book's signature and timestamp, and get_resolved_batch to read its forecasts and
    outcomes. An ungraded or unknown date is an error.

trading_date.description: The book's trading date, as YYYY-MM-DD. list_resolved_batches gives the graded dates.
trading_date.title: Trading Date

tools.name: verify_batch
tools.title: Verification record

tools.description:
Get a resolved book's portfolio: market-cap-weighted vs SPY ("cap", the default, the portfolio the ledger's
    verdict grades) or equal-weighted vs RSP ("equal"), with each long pick's weight and graded return, the book
    return, the benchmark return and its evidence, alpha and verdict. Equal weights always pair with RSP and cap weights
    with SPY. Per prediction, books serve the two as equal_weight and market_cap_weight; never read a pick's cap_weight
    as either without checking inference_metadata.weighting. Use this for one book's result, and get_simulation_nav for
    the running portfolio across books. An ungraded or unknown date is an error.

trading_date.description: The book's trading date, as YYYY-MM-DD. list_resolved_batches gives the graded dates.
trading_date.title: Trading Date

weighting.description: "cap" for market-cap weights against SPY (the default), or "equal" for equal weights against RSP.
weighting.title: Weighting

tools.name: get_book_portfolio
tools.title: Book portfolio

tools.description:
Find the developer guides and site pages that match a few words. Each
    hit carries the page title, its canonical URL and a short excerpt. Use this
    for how Timefire works and what its terms mean, not for record data. No
    match returns an empty list, so try other words.

query.description: A few words to search for, at most 8 words and 200 characters.
query.title: Query

limit.description: Most pages to return, 1 to 20. Default 5.
limit.title: Limit

tools.name: search_docs
tools.title: Search the docs

tools.description:
Get the paper portfolio's daily value (NAV), market-cap-weighted vs SPY ("cap", the default) or equal-weighted
    vs RSP ("equal"), with both benchmarks on every row. There is one row per resolved trading day. The series stops at
    the newest date by which every book is revealed, because a later value holds positions from books still sealed.
    Use this for portfolio value over time, and get_simulation_trades for the trades behind it.

from_date.description: Earliest date to include, as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for no lower bound.
from_date.title: From Date

to_date.description: Latest date to include, as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for no upper bound.
to_date.title: To Date

weighting.description: "cap" for market-cap weights against SPY (the default), or "equal" for equal weights against RSP.
weighting.title: Weighting

tools.name: get_simulation_nav
tools.title: Portfolio value

tools.description:
Get the paper portfolio's closed trades from resolved books, newest first, market-cap-weighted ("cap", the
    default) or equal-weighted ("equal"): the two trade at the same prices and differ in weight, and so in size and
    P&L. Open positions never appear. Date bounds apply to the day a trade opened; narrow them to see past the limit.
    Use this for individual trades, and get_simulation_nav for portfolio value.

from_date.description: Earliest date to include, as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for no lower bound.
from_date.title: From Date

to_date.description: Latest date to include, as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for no upper bound.
to_date.title: To Date

limit.description: Most trades to return, 1 to 500. Default 500. Older trades are cut off; there is no paging.
limit.title: Limit

weighting.description: "cap" for market-cap weights against SPY (the default), or "equal" for equal weights against RSP.
weighting.title: Weighting

tools.name: get_simulation_trades
tools.title: Portfolio trades

tools.description:
Get the stored evidence behind one stock's forecast in a graded book: its rank, side, market regime, 5- and
    20-day lookback returns, news items and notes. Use this to see the context a stock was ranked in, and
    get_stock_resolved_history to find which books hold it. An ungraded date, or a ticker not in that book, is an
    error.

trading_date.description: The book's trading date, as YYYY-MM-DD. list_resolved_batches gives the graded dates.
trading_date.title: Trading Date

ticker.description: Stock ticker, for example AAPL. Upper or lower case both work.
ticker.title: Ticker

tools.name: explain_resolved_prediction
tools.title: Explain a prediction
